newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols bid as spot hovers near highs.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols bid as spot hovers near highs.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options stayed well bid in cautious U.S. trading as the spot greenback hovered slightly below recent highs, dealers said.

The dollar/yen volatility curve was back into slight inversion, with the front end bolstered as the dollar drifted within striking distance of last week's four-year high at 124.72 yen and the psychologically important 125.00 yen.
"We're just short of 125 yen right now, and that's a very sensitive level," said Kyoko Hiramatsu, a senior dealer at Bank of Yokohama in New York.

One-month dollar/yen implied volatility stood at 11.4/11.7 percent at U.S. midsession, up from 10.4/10.6 percent late on Wednesday. One-year was at 11.3/11.5 percent, up some 0.7 point, while one-week was pegged at about 14.0/15.0 percent.
Traders said the inversion, in the face of a three-day weekend coming up, reflected the market's nervousness.

Shorter-dated options tend to come under pressure before a long weekend due to their steep time decay. But they were supported now by fear the dollar would stampede above 125 yen -- a barrier price for a lot of exotic options built up after last weekend's Group of Seven (G7) meeting, traders said.
At that meeting, the G7 industrial countries declared the dollar's correction from its 1995 lows was over, but the market has stayed generally bullish on the dollar.
Dollar/mark volatilities were also buoyant as the dollar hovered just below 1.69 marks after hitting a fresh 34-month high of 1.6935 marks on Wednesday.
One-month dollar/mark stood at 10.6/10.8 percent, up a quarter point from late Wednesday levels. The curve remained steeply inverted, with six-month and one-year at around 9.7/9.9 percent.
Traders said there was talk of a large exotic option barrier at 1.70 or 1.71 marks and that a frantic tug-of-war was expected as the dollar approached those levels.
"Spot's been moving a lot," said a German bank dealer in New York. "And with the Dow at 7,000 and what not, it (front-end volatility) is staying bid."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average of U.S. blue-chips briefly reached an all-time high of 7,000.89 earlier.
Traders said the U.S. Treasury's refunding auctions this week appeared to be proceeding fairly well, although concerns persisted that there could be some hangover later on.
Results of the $10 billion 30-year bond auction, the last of the three-legged refunding, was due out later in the day.

Elsewhere, sterling/mark continued drawing interest as the pound slid from early Wednesday's 52-month high of 2.7685 marks to a low today of 2.7315. British Chancellor of Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's comment that the sterling's recent strength would have "a very deflationary effect" on Britain's economy triggered pound selling, traders said.
One-month sterling/mark volatilities stood at 10.5/10.9 percent, near unchanged from Wednesday but off a quarter point from overnight highs.
